title: Common Go Interview Scenarios
intro: Common Go interview scenarios for freshers are the practical 'what does this code do?' and 'spot the bug' questions that differentiate candidates who have written real Go from those who have only read about it. This module covers seven scenario categories: goroutine vs thread (when to use a goroutine, the classic 'print numbers 1 to 10 concurrently' problem and why it requires sync), channel direction (what does chan<- T mean in a function signature and why you'd use it), interface vs concrete type (when a function should accept an io.Writer vs a *os.File), pointer vs value receiver (the method set gotcha with pointer receivers and interface satisfaction), the nil map panic (writing to a nil map panics; reading returns zero — how to prevent both), defer ordering (LIFO execution, the argument evaluation timing that catches everyone), and error handling scenarios (when to return nil, when to wrap, when to use a sentinel). Every scenario is a runnable Go program the interviewer will put in front of you.
